part.Name: Description
part.Short: Road-worn and rumor-led, they carry everything they own: a bedroll, an empty skin, and the name of a place where thirst is shared.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Lashed poles and borrowed planks. Somebody's promise is being kept, plank by plank.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Casks in a cradle of watervine rope. The whole settlement is counted here, dram by dram.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A tin-lined belly sunk to its rim in the earth. When it is full, the whole town sleeps easier; when it rings hollow, everyone hears it.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Rope-sprung and blanket-soft by local standards. It smells of road dust and relief.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Split logs worn smooth by sitting. The best arguments of the settlement happen here, and one or two of the marriages.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: An uncut stone with a cup-shaped hollow worn into its crown. Whatever is poured there is gone by morning, and no one asks where.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: A salvaged cradle of chrome and gut-wire, cranked by whoever has the shift. Set your cells on it and go eat; they will be full when you come back.

part.Name: Description
part.Short: Hammered from tin and older promises, it holds just enough water to make strangers into kin. Whoever fills it and pours may found a place worth thirsting for.
